name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz shut; more ships hit 10–11 Nov
summary: Ships hit by projectiles near Hormuz on 10–11 Nov and Iran claims mine strikes; traffic remains well below normal
state: UKMTO and Ambrey reported ships hit by projectiles north-east of Lima, Oman, on 10 and 11 Nov, one left disabled, and ADNOC confirmed a vessel damaged in UAE waters (Riviera). Iran said on 11 Nov the strait stays shut until its conditions are met, and the IRGC says tankers hit mines; this is unverified (Al Jazeera). Reuters figures cited by Gulf News count 10 attacks in November by 11 Nov after 37 in October. Materially impeded Hormuz traffic sets the Alert.
for_you: Disruption at Hormuz affects oil, LNG and container shipping costs and delivery times, which tend to feed through to fuel and goods prices. Seafarers and travellers in the Gulf region should follow UKMTO guidance and FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded: attacks on ships continued on 10–11 Nov and Iran says the strait stays shut

sources.title: Riviera — Tankers hit by projectiles in Strait of Hormuz; Iran reports further mine strikes
Gulf News — Why is Iran attacking tankers during peace talks?
Al Jazeera — Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
